title: Dreamcatcher: Remembering What Surprises a World Model in Video Streams
title_zh: Dreamcatcher：记住视频流中令世界模型意外的内容
abstract_en: As live video streams grow longer, repeatedly encoding and processing their full histories becomes increasingly costly. Answering questions as they arrive therefore calls for visual memory built in one pass before future questions are known. Existing methods mainly keep tokens that differ from earlier ones or match surrogate queries fixed in advance. Without modeling world dynamics, these criteria struggle to tell subtle surprising details from expected change. We introduce Dreamcatcher, a training-free framework and, to our knowledge, the first to use predictive signals from an independently pretrained, frozen video world model for online memory formation in streaming video question answering. Conditioned on recent history, the world model predicts incoming features using learned world priors. Its normalized prediction errors yield temporal and spatial surprisal signals that guide online segmentation and the retention of a frozen Video-LLM's native visual tokens, balancing surprising details with broad visual coverage under budgets that decay with segment age. At query time, an evidence gate admits a segment from a similarity-based shortlist only when the Video-LLM judges that it adds evidence for the question beyond the current view. We evaluate Dreamcatcher on three streaming and three offline long-video benchmarks. On OVO-Bench, Dreamcatcher achieves the highest overall accuracy among the compared training-free methods for each of four frozen Video-LLMs, reaching 78.9% with Qwen3.8-27B. With the three Qwen Video-LLMs, it also reduces average input tokens for answer generation by more than 80% relative to their base models at 1 fps.
abstract_zh: 随着实时视频流不断延长，反复编码和处理完整历史的成本越来越高。为了随时回答尚未出现的问题，系统需要在单遍处理视频时构建视觉记忆。现有方法主要保留与历史内容差异较大、或与预设代理查询匹配的 token，但由于缺乏对世界动态的建模，难以区分细微的意外细节与可预期的变化。Dreamcatcher 是一个无需训练的框架；据作者所知，它首次利用独立预训练并冻结的视频世界模型的预测信号，为流式视频问答在线构建记忆。世界模型根据近期历史预测即将到来的视觉特征，将归一化预测误差转化为时间和空间上的惊异度（surprisal），用于引导在线分段和保留冻结 Video-LLM 的原生视觉 token。在随片段变旧而递减的预算下，系统兼顾意外细节与整体视觉覆盖。回答问题时，系统先按相似度筛选候选片段，再由 Video-LLM 判断片段能否提供当前画面之外的相关证据，仅在能提供额外证据时纳入。实验覆盖 3 个流式视频基准和 3 个离线长视频基准。在 OVO-Bench 上，Dreamcatcher 搭配 4 种冻结 Video-LLM 时，均在所比较的免训练方法中取得最高总体准确率，其中 Qwen3.8-27B 达到 78.9%。在 1 fps 下，搭配 3 种 Qwen Video-LLM 时，生成答案所需的平均输入 token 数较各自基础模型减少超过 80%。
key_points_zh: 无需预知问题或额外训练，即可单遍构建流式视频记忆。
用冻结世界模型的归一化预测误差衡量时空惊异度，区分难以预测的细节与可预期的变化，并据此分段、保留视觉 token。
记忆预算随片段变旧而递减，在有限预算内兼顾意外细节与整体视觉覆盖。
检索先按相似度筛选，再通过证据门控，仅纳入能为问题补充当前画面之外证据的片段。
在 OVO-Bench 上，4 种冻结骨干均在所比较的免训练方法中取得最高总体准确率，Qwen3.8-27B 达到 78.9%；在 1 fps 下，3 种 Qwen 骨干的平均答题输入 token 数均较各自基础模型减少超过 80%。
